content.content:
DMS Greeter - a greetd login screen with the Dux Shell aesthetic.

Invoked from greetd as: dms-greeter --command COMPOSITOR

Usage:
  dms-greeter [flags]
  dms-greeter [command]

Available Commands:
  completion       Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  enable           Enable DMS greeter in greetd config
  help             Help about any command
  install          Install and configure DMS greeter
  kill             Kill running dms-greeter processes
  restart          Restart the running dms-greeter instance
  run              Launch dms-greeter (backend + UI)
  status           Check greeter sync status
  sync             Sync DMS theme and settings with greeter
  uninstall        Remove DMS greeter configuration and restore previous display manager
  unlink           Stop syncing this user's DMS settings to the greeter
  version          Show version information

Flags:
      --cache-dir string               Cache directory for greeter data (default "/var/cache/dms-greeter")
      --command string                 Compositor to use (niri, hyprland, sway, scroll, miracle, mango, labwc, or aqueous)
  -C, --config string                  Custom compositor config file
      --debug                          Leave compositor output on the greeter's own stdout/stderr instead of journald
  -h, --help                           help for dms-greeter
      --no-save-session                Alias for --remember-last-session false
      --no-save-username               Alias for --remember-last-user false
  -p, --path string                    Quickshell config name or absolute path (deprecated; the embedded UI is the default)
      --remember-last-session string   Persist selected session to greeter memory (true/false, default: from settings.json)
      --remember-last-user string      Persist last successful username to greeter memory (true/false, default: from settings.json)
  -c, --shell-dir string               Path to a UI config dir (containing shell.qml) to use instead of the embedded UI (env: DMS_GREETER_SHELL_DIR)

Use "dms-greeter [command] --help" for more information about a command.
== greetd config:
[terminal]
# The VT to run the greeter on. Can be "next", "current" or a number
# designating the VT.
vt = 1

# The default session, also known as the greeter.
[default_session]

# `agreety` is the bundled agetty/login-lookalike. You can replace `/bin/sh`
# with whatever you want started, such as `sway`.
command = "agreety --cmd /bin/sh"

# The user to run the command as. The privileges this user must have depends
# on the greeter. A graphical greeter may for example require the user to be
# in the `video` group.
user = "greetd"
== pam greetd:
#%PAM-1.0

content.content:
```bash
echo 'repository=https://void.duxlabs.dev/dux-repo/current' | sudo tee /etc/xbps.d/dux.conf
sudo xbps-install -S dux-greeter
# sudo xbps-install -S dux-greeter-git   # master snapshots; Conflicts with stable
```

The packages create the greeter user (via `systemd-sysusers` for atomic/immutable compatibility, with package script fallback), set up directories and permissions, and apply SELinux contexts where relevant.

After installing from any package:

```bash
dms-greeter enable   # point greetd at dms-greeter
dms-greeter sync     # sync your DMS theme to the login screen
```

Or run `dms-greeter install` for interactive setup - it installs greetd where needed and writes `/etc/greetd/config.toml` for you.

## Usage

greetd runs the greeter through `/etc/greetd/config.toml`:

```toml
[terminal]
vt = 1

[default_session]
user = "greeter"
command = "/usr/bin/dms-greeter --command niri"
```

The launcher takes care of the compositor side:

```bash
dms-greeter --command niri
dms-greeter --command hyprland
dms-greeter --command sway
dms-greeter --command mangowc
dms-greeter --command aqueous
dms-greeter --command aqueous -C /etc/greetd/aqueous.toml
dms-greeter --command niri -C /path/to/custom-niri.kdl
dms-greeter --command niri --remember-last-user false --remember-last-session false
```

## Configuration

### Compositor

# Sets up Hyprland + DMS from this folder, also on a fresh Fedora install (Workstation or a
# minimal install): installs the missing packages (DMS, Hyprland, Alacritty, fish, plus the

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sets up Hyprland + DMS from this folder, also on a fresh Fedora install: installs the missing
# packages (DMS, Hyprland, Alacritty, fish...), then restores the saved config.
# Before overwriting anything, it backs up the current config to ~/.config-backups/<date>.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CFG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}"
STATE="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}"
BACKUP="$HOME/.config-backups/$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
# Claude Code keeps sessions per directory, named after its path with non-alphanumerics as "-"
CLAUDE_PROJECT="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects/$(printf '%s' "$REPO" | sed 's/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/-/g')"
# COPRs: DMS (enabling it also enables its dependency repo avengemedia/danklinux, which
# ships quickshell, matugen, dgop, danksearch...) and Hyprland (the one recommended by the
# Hyprland wiki for Fedora)
DMS_COPR="avengemedia/dms"
HYPR_COPR="lionheartp/Hyprland"
HYPR_REPO_ID="copr:copr.fedorainfracloud.org:lionheartp:Hyprland"
# Installed with weak deps (DMS recommends cava, qt6ct, qt6-qtmultimedia...).
# breeze-icon-theme: breeze-dark is one of the fallbacks of the Sweet-Red icon theme.
PACKAGES=(dms danksearch matugen dgop alacritty fish zoxide gcr gnome-keyring
    breeze-icon-theme xdg-desktop-portal-gtk)
# Installed without weak deps: they pull a bar, a launcher and kitty, which DMS already covers
HYPR_PACKAGES=(hyprland xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland)

# Packages: only the missing ones, so on an already set up system nothing is asked
missing() { for p in "$@"; do rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "$p"; done; }
mapfile -t need < <(missing "${PACKAGES[@]}")
mapfile -t need_hypr < <(missing "${HYPR_PACKAGES[@]}")
if (( ${#need[@]} + ${#need_hypr[@]} )); then
    echo "Installing ${need[*]} ${need_hypr[*]} (needs sudo)"
    # dnf copr and dnf config-manager come from dnf5-plugins
    rpm -q dnf5-plugins >/dev/null || sudo dnf install -y dnf5-plugins
    sudo dnf copr enable -y "$DMS_COPR"
    sudo dnf copr enable -y "$HYPR_COPR"
    # The Hyprland COPR also ships quickshell and matugen; keep the versions DMS depends on
    sudo dnf config-manager setopt "$HYPR_REPO_ID.excludepkgs=quickshell,matugen"
    if (( ${#need[@]} )); then sudo dnf install -y "${need[@]}"; fi
    if (( ${#need_hypr[@]} )); then
        sudo dnf install -y --setopt=install_weak_deps=False "${need_hypr[@]}"
    fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sets up Hyprland + DMS from this folder, also on a fresh Fedora install (Workstation or a
# minimal install): installs the missing packages (DMS, Hyprland, Alacritty, fish, plus the
# desktop basics a minimal install lacks: graphics, audio, fonts, login screen...), then
# restores the saved config.
# Before overwriting anything, it backs up the current config to ~/.config-backups/<date>.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CFG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}"
STATE="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}"
BACKUP="$HOME/.config-backups/$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
# Claude Code keeps sessions per directory, named after its path with non-alphanumerics as "-"
CLAUDE_PROJECT="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects/$(printf '%s' "$REPO" | sed 's/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/-/g')"
# COPRs: DMS (enabling it also enables its dependency repo avengemedia/danklinux, which
# ships quickshell, matugen, dgop, danksearch...) and Hyprland (the one recommended by the
# Hyprland wiki for Fedora)
DMS_COPR="avengemedia/dms"
HYPR_COPR="lionheartp/Hyprland"
HYPR_REPO_ID="copr:copr.fedorainfracloud.org:lionheartp:Hyprland"
# Installed with weak deps (DMS recommends cava, qt6ct, qt6-qtmultimedia...).
# breeze-icon-theme: breeze-dark is one of the fallbacks of the Sweet-Red icon theme.
PACKAGES=(dms danksearch matugen dgop alacritty fish zoxide gcr gnome-keyring
    breeze-icon-theme xdg-desktop-portal-gtk)
# Desktop basics that Fedora Workstation has and a minimal install doesn't:
# graphics (Intel/AMD; NVIDIA needs RPM Fusion), audio (DMS volume uses PipeWire), battery and
# power profiles, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, fonts (DMS uses Fira Code as monospace), xdg tools
PACKAGES+=(mesa-dri-drivers mesa-vulkan-drivers pipewire pipewire-pulseaudio wireplumber
    upower power-profiles-daemon NetworkManager-wifi bluez polkit xdg-utils xdg-user-dirs
    google-noto-sans-vf-fonts google-noto-sans-mono-vf-fonts google-noto-color-emoji-fonts
    fira-code-fonts)
# Login screen, only when there is no display manager yet (a minimal install has none;
# on Workstation GDM is kept): greetd with the DMS greeter
if [[ ! -e /etc/systemd/system/display-manager.service ]]; then
    PACKAGES+=(greetd dms-greeter)
    SETUP_GREETER=1
fi
# Installed without weak deps: they pull a bar, a launcher and kitty, which DMS already covers
HYPR_PACKAGES=(hyprland xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland)

# Packages: only the missing ones, so on an already set up system nothing is asked.
# Checked by capability, so replacements count (e.g. mesa-vulkan-drivers-freeworld).
missing() { for p in "$@"; do rpm -q --whatprovides "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "$p"; done; }
mapfile -t need < <(missing "${PACKAGES[@]}")
mapfile -t need_hypr < <(missing "${HYPR_PACKAGES[@]}")
if (( ${#need[@]} + ${#need_hypr[@]} )); then
    echo "Installing ${need[*]} ${need_hypr[*]} (needs sudo)"
    # dnf copr and dnf config-manager come from dnf5-plugins
    rpm -q dnf5-plugins >/dev/null || sudo dnf install -y dnf5-plugins
    sudo dnf copr enable -y "$DMS_COPR"
    sudo dnf copr enable -y "$HYPR_COPR"
    # The Hyprland COPR also ships quickshell and matugen; keep the versions DMS depends on
    sudo dnf config-manager setopt "$HYPR_REPO_ID.excludepkgs=quickshell,matugen"
    if (( ${#need[@]} )); then sudo dnf install -y "${need[@]}"; fi
    if (( ${#need_hypr[@]} )); then
        sudo dnf install -y --setopt=install_weak_deps=False "${need_hypr[@]}"
    fi
fi

# Bluetooth is not enabled on a minimal install
if ! systemctl is-enabled -q bluetooth.service 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Enabling Bluetooth (needs sudo)"
    sudo systemctl enable bluetooth.service
fi

# Login screen (minimal install): greetd runs the DMS greeter on Hyprland, and the system
# boots to the graphical target. greetd's Fedora PAM file already unlocks gnome-keyring.
if [[ -n "${SETUP_GREETER:-}" ]]; then
    echo "Setting up greetd + dms-greeter as the login screen (needs sudo)"
    sudo tee /etc/greetd/config.toml >/dev/null <<'EOF'
# Written by hyprland-dms-config/restore.sh: DMS greeter on Hyprland
[terminal]
vt = 1

[default_session]
user = "greeter"
command = "/usr/bin/dms-greeter --command hyprland"
EOF
    sudo systemctl enable greetd.service
    sudo systemctl set-default graphical.target
fi

# Validate the Hyprland config before touching anything
Hyprland --verify-config -c "$REPO/hypr/hyprland.lua" 2>&1 | grep -q 'config ok' || {

    Hyprland --verify-config -c "$REPO/hypr/hyprland.lua" >&2
    exit 1

mkdir -p "$BACKUP/state"
for d in hypr dms alacritty fish; do

done
[[ -f "$STATE/dms/session.json" ]] && cp "$STATE/dms/session.json" "$BACKUP/state/"
mkdir -p "$BACKUP/cursor"
[[ -f "$HOME/.icons/default/index.theme" ]] && cp "$HOME/.icons/default/index.theme" "$BACKUP/cursor/"
[[ -f "$CFG/environment.d/90-cursor.conf" ]] && cp "$CFG/environment.d/90-cursor.conf" "$BACKUP/cursor/"
[[ -d "$HOME/.icons/Hacked-Red" ]] && cp -a "$HOME/.icons/Hacked-Red" "$BACKUP/cursor/"
for t in "$REPO/icons/"*/; do

cp "$REPO/hypr/dms/"*.lua "$CFG/hypr/dms/"
[[ -d "$REPO/hypr/scripts" ]] && cp -r "$REPO/hypr/scripts" "$CFG/hypr/"

# systemd user service; `dms setup` normally adds this link)

cp -r "$REPO/dms/config/." "$CFG/dms/"
cp "$REPO/dms/state/session.json" "$STATE/dms/"
systemctl --user add-wants hyprland-session.target dms.service

cp "$REPO/alacritty/"*.toml "$CFG/alacritty/"

# fish (installed above, with zoxide used by config.fish): copy the config, make it the default shell
mkdir -p "$CFG/fish"
cp -r "$REPO/fish/." "$CFG/fish/"
fish_path="$(command -v fish)"
if [[ "$(getent passwd "$(id -un)" | cut -d: -f7)" != "$fish_path" ]]; then
    echo "Setting fish as the default shell (asks for your password)"
    chsh -s "$fish_path"
fi

cp "$REPO/cursor/index.theme" "$HOME/.icons/default/"
cp "$REPO/cursor/90-cursor.conf" "$CFG/environment.d/"
rm -rf "$HOME/.icons/Hacked-Red"
cp -a "$REPO/cursor/Hacked-Red" "$HOME/.icons/"

    rm -rf "$HOME/.icons/$(basename "$t")"
    cp -a "$t" "$HOME/.icons/"
done

cp "$REPO/ssh-agent/90-ssh-agent.conf" "$CFG/environment.d/"

if [[ -d "$REPO/claude" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$CLAUDE_PROJECT"
    cp -r "$REPO/claude/." "$CLAUDE_PROJECT/"
fi

# Wallpaper: copied to the path session.json expects if it is missing
wp="$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get("wallpaperPath",""))' "$REPO/dms/state/session.json")"
if [[ -n "$wp" && ! -f "$wp" && -f "$REPO/wallpaper/$(basename "$wp")" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$wp")"
    cp "$REPO/wallpaper/$(basename "$wp")" "$wp"
fi

echo "Done. Hyprland reloads its config on its own (or run: hyprctl reload); for DMS: dms restart"

input.command:
cd ~/hyprland-dms-config && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='README.md'; s=open(p).read()
i=s.index('## Fresh install'); j=s.index('## How DMS is started')
new='''## Fresh install

Works on a fresh **Fedora Workstation** or a **minimal Fedora install** (e.g. the
"Minimal Install" of the Everything netinstaller, which boots to a text console).

```sh
sudo dnf install git     # a minimal install has no git
git clone https://github.com/mirko-geno/hyprland-dms-config.git ~/hyprland-dms-config
cd ~/hyprland-dms-config
./restore.sh   # asks for sudo (packages, login screen) and your password (chsh to fish)
```

The repo is private: cloning over HTTPS asks for a GitHub username and a personal access
token (or set up an SSH key first and use the `git@github.com:` URL).

- **Workstation:** log out and pick **Hyprland** in GDM (gear icon at the bottom right).
  GDM is kept; the DMS greeter is not installed.
- **Minimal install:** reboot. There was no display manager, so `restore.sh` sets up greetd
  with the DMS greeter (themed like the desktop) and makes the system boot to the
  graphical target.

`restore.sh` installs only the packages that are missing (checked by what they provide, so
replacements like `mesa-vulkan-drivers-freeworld` count), so on a system that is already
set up it does not ask for sudo:

| Source | Packages |
|---|---|
| [`avengemedia/dms`](https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/coprs/avengemedia/dms/) COPR (+ its dependency repo `avengemedia/danklinux`) | `dms` (pulls `dms-cli`, `quickshell`), `danksearch`, `matugen`, `dgop`; `dms-greeter` (login screen, minimal install only) |
| [`lionheartp/Hyprland`](https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/coprs/lionheartp/Hyprland/) COPR (recommended by the Hyprland wiki) | `hyprland`, `xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland` |
| Fedora | `alacritty`, `fish`, `zoxide`, `gcr`, `gnome-keyring`, `breeze-icon-theme`, `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` (and `dnf5-plugins` for `dnf copr`) |
| Fedora: desktop basics a minimal install lacks | graphics `mesa-dri-drivers`, `mesa-vulkan-drivers`; audio `pipewire`, `pipewire-pulseaudio`, `wireplumber`; battery/power `upower`, `power-profiles-daemon`; `NetworkManager-wifi`, `bluez`; `polkit`, `xdg-utils`, `xdg-user-dirs`; fonts `google-noto-sans-vf-fonts`, `google-noto-sans-mono-vf-fonts`, `google-noto-color-emoji-fonts`, `fira-code-fonts` (DMS monospace font); `greetd` (minimal install only) |

- DMS packages are installed with weak deps (DMS recommends `cava`, `qt6ct`,
  `qt6-qtmultimedia`...). Hyprland is installed without them: they would pull `nwg-panel`,
  `wofi` and `kitty`, which DMS already covers.
- The Hyprland COPR also ships `quickshell` and `matugen`; they are excluded from it
  (`excludepkgs`) so the versions DMS depends on are kept.
- DMS runs as the `dms.service` systemd user service; `restore.sh` adds it to
  `hyprland-session.target` (what `dms setup` does), so it starts with the Hyprland session.
- Bluetooth (`bluetooth.service`) is enabled if it isn't.
- Login screen (only when `/etc/systemd/system/display-manager.service` does not exist):
  `restore.sh` writes `/etc/greetd/config.toml` (user `greeter`, command
  `/usr/bin/dms-greeter --command hyprland`), enables `greetd.service`, sets
  `graphical.target` as default and runs `dms-greeter sync` to copy the DMS theme and
  wallpaper to it. Fedora's `/etc/pam.d/greetd` already unlocks gnome-keyring at login.
- NVIDIA GPUs need the proprietary driver from RPM Fusion, which is not handled here
  (Intel/AMD work with Mesa).
- Apps (browser, file manager, editor...) are not installed by `restore.sh`.
- Untested on an actual minimal install yet: try it in a VM first.

Manual equivalent of the package part (Workstation):

```sh
sudo dnf copr enable avengemedia/dms
sudo dnf copr enable lionheartp/Hyprland
sudo dnf config-manager setopt "copr:copr.fedorainfracloud.org:lionheartp:Hyprland.excludepkgs=quickshell,matugen"
sudo dnf install dms danksearch matugen dgop alacritty fish zoxide gcr gnome-keyring breeze-icon-theme xdg-desktop-portal-gtk
sudo dnf install --setopt=install_weak_deps=False hyprland xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland
systemctl --user add-wants hyprland-session.target dms.service
```

'''
s=s[:i]+new+s[j:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n 'graphical session' README.md; ./backup.sh >/dev/null; git status --short
